_meta.indication: Treatment of EGFR-expressing, metastatic colorectal carcinoma with disease progression on or following fluoropyrimidine-, oxaliplatin-, and irinotecan-containing chemotherapy regimens.

pivotal_trials.trial_name: Study 20020408 (ABX-EGF plus Best Supportive Care Versus Best Supportive Care)
pivotal_trials.design: Open-label, multinational, randomized (1:1), controlled trial of panitumumab 6 mg/kg every 2 weeks plus best supportive care (BSC) versus BSC alone, stratified by ECOG performance status and geographic region.
pivotal_trials.population: Patients with EGFR-expressing metastatic colorectal cancer who had disease progression during or after fluoropyrimidine-, irinotecan-, and oxaliplatin-containing chemotherapy.
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Progression-free survival (PFS) was the primary efficacy endpoint.
pivotal_trials.result: Statistically significant prolongation of PFS with panitumumab + BSC vs BSC alone (hazard ratio 0.544 [95% CI 0.445, 0.665]; stratified log-rank p < 0.0001); mean PFS 96 days vs 60 days. No improvement in overall survival was demonstrated.

nct_ctgov.title: Evaluating Panitumumab (ABX-EGF) Plus Best Supportive Care Versus Best Supportive Care in Patients With Metastatic Colorectal Cancer

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions include dermatologic toxicity (reported in 90% of patients; severe in 16%), fatigue (26% vs 15% BSC), abdominal pain (25% vs 17%), nausea (23% vs 16%), diarrhea (21% vs 11%), and hypomagnesemia. Most serious events include severe infusion reactions (~1%) and pulmonary fibrosis (<1%, 2/1467).
target_moa: Panitumumab is a human IgG2 kappa monoclonal antibody that binds specifically to the human Epidermal Growth Factor Receptor (EGFR) and competitively inhibits binding of EGFR ligands, preventing ligand-induced receptor autophosphorylation and activation, resulting in inhibition of cell growth and induction of apoptosis.
modality: mAb (recombinant human IgG2 kappa monoclonal antibody)

boxed_warning.content: Boxed warning for Dermatologic Toxicity (reported in 89% of patients; severe in 12% on monotherapy) and Infusion Reactions (severe in approximately 1% of patients).

companion_dx_detail: EGFR tumor expression was determined using the Dako EGFR pharmDx test kit; detection of EGFR protein expression is necessary for selection of patients appropriate for Vectibix therapy.

advisory_committee.vote: An Advisory Committee meeting was not considered necessary for this product (though an earlier ODAC committee had recommended that PFS is reasonably likely to predict an effect on overall survival and is an acceptable endpoint in support of accelerated approval).

description.text: Added indication for Vectibix in combination with sotorasib for KRAS G12C-mutated mCRC after prior fluoropyrimidine-, oxaliplatin-, and irinotecan-based chemotherapy

citations.quote: This Prior Approval supplemental biologics license application adds a new indication of Vectibix, in combination with sotorasib, for the treatment of adult patients with KRAS G12C-mutated metastatic colorectal cancer (mCRC), as determined by an FDA approved test, who have received prior treatment with fluoropyrimidine-, oxaliplatin-, and irinotecan-based chemotherapy. It also adds the following statement to the Limitations of Use: "Vectibix is not indicated for the treatment of patients with RAS-mutant mCRC unless used in combination with sotorasib in KRAS G12C-mutated mCRC."
